findings.claim: Physics and Chemistry remain strong foundational-domain candidates, but their shared bridge zones such as chemical physics, condensed matter and materials require separate identities rather than exclusive parentage.
Materials science and engineering is a major interdisciplinary bridge domain coupling fundamental structure/property inquiry with design, synthesis, processing and technological intervention.
Biology is intrinsically multi-axis: molecular/cellular scale, organismal integration, evolutionary processes and ecological systems cannot be represented as one simple branch hierarchy.

Engineering is best modeled as an intervention/design/realization domain; design and systems engineering are cross-cutting methodological/integrative axes rather than ordinary natural-science subfields.
Philosophy and History deserve distinct first-class identities with different epistemic roles; Historical/Symbolic is therefore a family view, not one domain.
Basic biomedical science is a foundational bridge into medicine, while medicine/health as a whole is translational/professional and should not be admitted wholesale as a foundational root.

Agriculture is an applied intervention/system domain drawing on life, Earth, chemistry, engineering and social/economic inputs; soil science is a major cross-boundary subspace rather than merely an agricultural topic.

negativeFindings.claim: NSF Emerging Frontiers is an organizational/funding mechanism, not automatically a knowledge-domain identity.
NIH institute boundaries organized around diseases/body systems/missions must not be copied as a foundational biomedical ontology.
Engineering accreditation categories and NSF administrative sections do not mint canonical epistemic roots.
Composite humanities fields such as Classics must not be mistaken for primitive roots merely because they are institutionally established disciplines.

next: Whole-Foundational Topology Audit across Round1+2A+2B before any canonical-root admission or Ordivon coverage crosswalk.

normalizedSpaces.label: Physics
normalizedSpaces.rationale: APS maintains many physics subfields with cross-links to astronomy, biology, chemistry, materials and computation. Physics remains a major foundational-domain candidate but not a universal parent for every physically grounded field.

normalizedSpaces.label: Chemistry
normalizedSpaces.rationale: IUPAC organizes chemistry into multiple divisions including physical/biophysical, inorganic, organic/biomolecular, polymer, analytical, environment and health-related chemistry, supporting chemistry as a first-class domain with internal methodological and bridge subspaces.

normalizedSpaces.label: Condensed matter physics
normalizedSpaces.rationale: APS treats condensed matter as a major physics division while materials physics is separately represented; condensed matter therefore remains a major physics subspace with strong materials overlap.

normalizedSpaces.label: Chemical physics
normalizedSpaces.rationale: APS explicitly maintains Chemical Physics and IUPAC maintains Physical and Biophysical Chemistry, demonstrating a stable physics↔chemistry bridge rather than exclusive placement.

normalizedSpaces.label: Materials science and engineering
normalizedSpaces.rationale: NSF and MRS both characterize materials research as inherently interdisciplinary across physics, chemistry, biology and engineering, linking fundamental structure/property understanding to design, synthesis, processing and technological creation.

normalizedSpaces.label: Analytical chemistry
normalizedSpaces.rationale: IUPAC recognizes Analytical Chemistry as a distinct division. Its focus on measurement/characterization supports a chemistry subspace with methodological-axis character rather than a separate foundational root.

normalizedSpaces.label: Polymer science
normalizedSpaces.rationale: Polymer is independently organized in both IUPAC and APS, indicating a stable cross-domain identity spanning chemistry, physics and materials.

normalizedSpaces.label: Biology
normalizedSpaces.rationale: NSF BIO organizes fundamental biology from molecular/cellular through organismal and ecological/evolutionary scales, supporting biology as a first-class life-domain candidate with multiple orthogonal scales and processes.

normalizedSpaces.label: Molecular and cellular biosciences
normalizedSpaces.rationale: NSF MCB targets fundamental properties of living systems at atomic, molecular, subcellular and cellular scales; this is a major lower-scale biological subspace, not equivalent to biology as a whole.

normalizedSpaces.label: Organismal biology
normalizedSpaces.rationale: NSF IOS explicitly studies organisms as integrated units of biological organization, supporting organismal biology as a major system-level subspace.

normalizedSpaces.label: Evolutionary biology
normalizedSpaces.rationale: NSF Environmental Biology explicitly supports fundamental evolutionary research across biological entities and scales. Evolution is better modeled as a pervasive biological process axis plus major subspace than as one taxonomic branch among peers.

normalizedSpaces.label: Ecology
normalizedSpaces.rationale: NSF DEB covers species, populations, communities and ecosystems across scales, supporting ecology as a system-oriented life/environment bridge.

normalizedSpaces.label: Biological research infrastructure
normalizedSpaces.rationale: NSF DBI funds technologies, facilities and human/research infrastructure for fundamental biology. This should be represented as research infrastructure, not mistaken for a biological object-domain.

normalizedSpaces.label: Engineering
normalizedSpaces.rationale: NSF organizes engineering around chemical/bio/energy/transport, civil/mechanical/manufacturing, and electrical/communications/computing areas, while ABET distinguishes engineering from basic sciences. Engineering is therefore best represented as a design/intervention/realization domain rather than another natural-science object domain.

normalizedSpaces.label: Design
normalizedSpaces.rationale: The Design Society treats design as creation of artifacts and systems across physical, virtual, psychological, economic and social environments. Design is a cross-domain intervention axis, not reducible to engineering alone.

normalizedSpaces.label: Systems engineering
normalizedSpaces.rationale: INCOSE defines systems engineering as transdisciplinary and integrative across realization, use and retirement of engineered systems; it is a lifecycle integration method/domain rather than a single artifact-class branch.

normalizedSpaces.label: Manufacturing
normalizedSpaces.rationale: NSF engineering treats manufacturing together with civil/mechanical innovation and material/building technologies, supporting manufacturing as a realization/application domain rather than a foundational science root.

normalizedSpaces.label: Bioengineering
normalizedSpaces.rationale: NSF places bioengineering with engineering healthcare while NIH maintains biomedical imaging/bioengineering institutes; bioengineering is a strong biology↔medicine↔engineering bridge.

normalizedSpaces.label: Philosophy
normalizedSpaces.rationale: APA identifies metaphysics, epistemology, logic and ethics as central philosophical areas while emphasizing history, argument construction and expanding cross-disciplinary inquiry. Philosophy is not merely a historical-symbolic bucket.

normalizedSpaces.label: History
normalizedSpaces.rationale: AHA explicitly represents history as a distinct discipline centered on historical thinking and disciplined investigation/interpretation of the past, supporting first-class identity independent of generic humanities.

normalizedSpaces.label: Religious studies
normalizedSpaces.rationale: AAR frames its mission around academic study of religion across world traditions and methodologies. This supports a first-class comparative domain identity but not foundational-root admission in the current pre-social wave.

normalizedSpaces.label: Aesthetics
normalizedSpaces.rationale: ASA explicitly includes philosophical, scientific and theoretical studies of the arts and related experience, including psychology, sociology, anthropology and cultural history. Aesthetics is therefore a bridge identity rather than a philosophy-only child.

normalizedSpaces.label: Classics / Classical studies
normalizedSpaces.rationale: SCS defines Classics across languages, literatures, history, material culture, philosophy, law, religion and art of the ancient Mediterranean. It is a composite domain, not evidence for a universal foundational root.

normalizedSpaces.label: Basic biomedical sciences
normalizedSpaces.rationale: NIH NIGMS explicitly supports basic research on biological processes that underpins diagnosis, treatment and prevention, demonstrating a foundational biology↔medicine bridge distinct from clinical practice.

normalizedSpaces.label: Medicine and health sciences
normalizedSpaces.rationale: NIH organization is largely disease/body-system/health-mission oriented and spans basic, translational and clinical research. Medicine/health should not be imported wholesale as a foundational object-domain even though it contains foundational biomedical cores.

normalizedSpaces.label: Agricultural sciences and systems
normalizedSpaces.rationale: NIFA agricultural topics combine plants, animals, ecosystems, natural resources, technology, food systems and human/economic concerns. Agriculture is an intervention/system domain drawing on multiple foundations rather than a single foundational root.

normalizedSpaces.label: Soil science
normalizedSpaces.rationale: NIFA describes soil as a dynamic natural resource central to plant growth, air/water quality, ecosystems, climate, nutrient cycling and agriculture. Soil science is a strong Earth↔life↔chemistry↔agriculture bridge.

policies.administrativeBoundary: Funding/society/accreditation organization is evidence about field shape, not ontology authority.
policies.appliedBoundary: Applied/professional domains may contain foundational cores without becoming foundational roots wholesale.
policies.compositeFields: Institutionally stable composite disciplines are not automatically primitive roots.
policies.multiAxis: Scale, process, system, method and intervention relations may cross-cut discipline identities.
